'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Twenty-five people are killed and 14 injured after a bus overturned in [[Dawunt District]], [[Ethiopia]]. [https://thesudantimes.com/africa/deadly-bus-accident-in-northern-ethiopia-25-killed/ (The Sudan Times)]
*Four people are killed and five more injured in a [[stampede]] at [[Cambodia]]n businessman [[Sok Kong]]'s home in [[Phnom Penh]] as he was giving away food and money amid [[Lunar New Year]] celebrations. [https://apnews.com/article/cambodia-crowd-crush-killed-sok-kong-facdf0652f008fa1695283aae9f49078 (AP)]
*Nineteen vehicles figured in a pileup along the [[Yekaterinburg]]-[[Almaty]] highway near [[Aksu-Ayuly]], [[Kazakhstan]], [[Karaganda Region]], injuring six. [https://en.inform.kz/news/several-injured-in-massive-19-car-pile-up-in-karaganda-region-8ed368/ (Kazinform)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2024 Southport stabbing]]
**A court in [[Liverpool]], [[England]], sentences the man who was found guilty of killing three children and injuring 10 others in a [[mass stabbing]] in [[Southport]], [[Merseyside]], to [[life imprisonment]] with a minimum of 52 years in prison. [https://www.dw.com/en/uk-court-jails-southport-girls-murderer-to-52-years/a-71382959 (DW)]
*[[LGBTQ rights in Thailand]]
** [[Thailand]] becomes the 38th country and the first in [[Southeast Asia]] to legalize [[Same-sex marriage in Thailand|same-sex marriage]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/thailands-same-sex-marriage-law-2025-01-23/ (Reuters)]
*The [[International Criminal Court]] prosecutor requests [[arrest warrant]]s against Afghanistan's [[Taliban]] [[Supreme Leader of Afghanistan|supreme leader]] [[Hibatullah Akhundzada]] and Taliban [[Chief Justice of Afghanistan|chief justice]] [[Abdul Hakim Haqqani]], accusing them of [[crimes against humanity]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/icc-prosecutor-seeks-arrest-warrants-against-taliban-leaders-2025-01-23/ (Reuters)]
*[[Federal law enforcement in the United States|United States federal law enforcement]] and [[U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement|ICE]] agents arrest nearly 500 [[Illegal immigration to the United States|undocumented migrants]] with arrest warrants in [[sanctuary cities]], including in [[New Jersey]] and [[New York (state)|New York]]. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/world/article/ice-agents-arrest-hundreds-of-migrants-in-sanctuary-cities-including-new-york-city/ (CTV News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Second presidency of Donald Trump]]
**[[List of executive actions by Donald Trump|Executive actions by Donald Trump]]
***[[Declassification of Records Concerning the Assassinations of President John F. Kennedy, Senator Robert F. Kennedy, and the Reverend Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr.]]
****[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] signs an [[executive order]] to [[declassify]] files related to the [[Assassination of John F. Kennedy|assassinations of John F. Kennedy]], [[Assassination of Robert F. Kennedy|Robert F. Kennedy]] and [[Assassination of Martin Luther King Jr.|Martin Luther King Jr]]. [https://www.axios.com/2025/01/23/trump-classified-files-jfk-mlk-assassinations-executive-order (Axios)]
**[[State of Washington v. Trump (2025)]]
***[[United States federal judge|U.S. District Judge]] for [[United States District Court for the Western District of Washington|Washington]] [[John C. Coughenour]] temporarily blocks President Trump's [[Executive Order 14156|executive order]] attempting to end [[birthright citizenship in the United States|birthright citizenship]], calling it "blatantly [[Constitution of the United States|unconstitutional]]". [https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-judge-hear-states-bid-block-trump-birthright-citizenship-order-2025-01-23/ (Reuters)] [https://www.nytimes.com/2025/01/23/us/politics/judge-blocks-birthright-citizenship.html (''The New York Times'')]
**The [[United States Department of State|U.S. Department of State]] bans [[List of diplomatic missions of the United States|consular posts]] from flying any flags other than the [[Flag of the United States|U.S. flag]] as part of the [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] targeting several instances during the [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Biden administration]] when [[Rainbow flag (LGBTQ)|LGBTQ pride]] and [[Black Lives Matter|Black Lives Matter flag]]s were flown at embassies abroad. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/jan/23/trump-administration-bans-non-us-flags-from-being-flown-at-embassies (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2024 Irish general election]], [[Government of the 34th Dáil]]
**[[Fianna Fáil]] and [[Fine Gael]] form a [[coalition government]] with the backing of several [[Independent_politician_(Ireland)|independent TDs]]. Fianna Fáil leader [[Micheál Martin]] is elected as [[Taoiseach]], with Fine Gael leader [[Simon Harris]] as [[Tánaiste]]. [https://www.politico.eu/article/dublin-detente-micheal-martin-elected-prime-minister-after-opposition-showdown/ (Politico)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2025 Australian Open]]
**In [[tennis]], [[John Peers]] and [[Olivia Gadecki]], both from [[Australia]], defeats [[Kimberly Birrell]] and [[John-Patrick Smith]] 3-6, 6-4, 10-6, in the [[2025 Australian Open – Mixed doubles|mixed doubles final]] to win their first [[Australian Open]] title. [https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2025/jan/24/local-heroes-olivia-gadecki-and-john-peers-clinch-australian-open-mixed-doubles-title (''The Guardian'')]
